rv.q: If anything, this breathtakingly thrilling production by Jamie Lloyd - and the tour-de-force central performance by James McAvoy as the eponymous, big-nosed soldier-poet - have only become deeper and richer since the 2019 premiere.
McAvoy’s performance is glorious, stage-owning yet generous.
Once again, Lloyd proves he has a nose for a triumphant theatrical reinvention.

Writers are fighters and the word is everything in this firecracker show about passion, rejection, and the crazy genius of the spoken word. The rapiers, intrigue and censorship of Cardinal Richelieu’s Paris, circa 1640, are modernised as razor-sharp banter about love, sex, and – nudge, wink – cultural appropriation.
It’s a thrilling, moving revival with McAvoy outstanding as a man torn in two.

cn.t: Lloyd's radical, minimalist revival strips away the nose and period trappings, with McAvoy delivering a phenomenal, fiercely charismatic performance that deepens the play's themes of loneliness and communication.
